title: Reverse a Playlist in Groups of K
statement: A playlist is represented as a plain list `songs` in play order, conceptually chained like a singly linked list where each song only knows the one after it. Reverse the order of songs in each consecutive group of k songs. If the number of remaining songs at the end is fewer than k, leave that final partial group in its original order. Return the resulting playlist as a list. Solve it using the in-place linked-list group-reversal technique (reverse pointers within each window using O(1) extra space per group, not by slicing and calling a built-in reverse on the whole structure).
hints: This is the k-group reversal variant of the linked-list reversal pattern: reverse each full window of k nodes and leave a trailing short group untouched.
Only reverse a window if it has exactly k elements remaining; a shorter trailing window stays in its original order.
For each window [start, start+k), swap elements symmetrically from both ends inward (two-pointer in-place reversal) instead of building a new list with slicing.
